message.content:
I don’t have a way to directly probe your connection from here, but you can quickly check your current download/upload speeds yourself. Below are a few easy options you can try on a Windows machine:

---

## 1. Use the official Speedtest CLI (if you have it installed)

If you already have `speedtest-cli` (the command‑line client for speedtest.net) installed, just run:

```powershell
speedtest
```

If you don’t have it, you can install it with pip (Python’s package manager):

```powershell
pip install speedtest-cli
```

Once installed, run `speedtest` again and it will report download, upload, and ping.

---

## 2. Quick PowerShell test (download a known file)

If you prefer not to install anything, you can use PowerShell to download a test file and measure how long it takes. Here’s a one‑liner that downloads a 100 MB file from Hetzner’s speed test server and prints the elapsed time:

```powershell
Measure-Command { Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://speed.hetzner.de/100MB.bin' -OutFile 'C:\Temp\speedtest.bin' }
```

- **What it does**:  
  - `Measure-Command` measures the time taken by the block.  
  - `Invoke-WebRequest` downloads the file.  
  - The output will show something like `Days: 0 Hours: 0 Minutes: 0 Seconds: 12.3456789 Milliseconds: 0`.

- **How to interpret**:  
  - If the download took ~12 seconds for 100 MB, your download speed is roughly  
    \[
    \frac{100 \text{ MB}}{12 \text{ s}} \approx 8.3 \text{ MB/s} \approx 66 \text{ Mbps}
    \]
  - You can do a similar test for upload by uploading a file to a server that accepts uploads (though that’s a bit more involved).

---

## 3. Use a web browser

The simplest way is to visit a speed‑test website:

- [speedtest.net](https://www.speedtest.net/)
- [fast.com](https://fast.com/) (Netflix’s test)
- [speedof.me](https://speedof.me/)

Just open the site, click “Go” or “Start”, and it will automatically test your download and upload speeds.

---

## 4. Using Windows built‑in tools

If you want a quick look at your network adapter’s statistics:

```powershell
Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name "Ethernet"
```

This shows bytes received/sent per second, but it’s a snapshot of the current traffic, not a dedicated speed test.

---

### Quick Summary

| Method | What you need | How fast? |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| `speedtest-cli` | Python + pip | Full download/upload + ping |
| PowerShell download | PowerShell only | Rough estimate (download only) |
| Browser test | Web browser | Full test (download/upload/ping) |

Pick the one that feels easiest for you. If you run into any trouble or want to automate the test, let me know and I can help you write a small script!
